extraction.agency_name: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene Developmental Disabilities Administration
extraction.parent_department: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

findings.title: DDA incorrectly directed providers to collect an estimated $4.2 million annually from consumers for services that should have been paid for with State and federal funds. DDA believes that its administrative and financial costs to remedy this situation outweigh the potential benefits to the affected consumers.
findings.description: Prior to fiscal year 2015, DDA incorrectly directed providers to collect contribution to care (CTC) from Medicaid-eligible consumers for services that should have been paid by State and federal funds. DDA management advised that improper collections had occurred for many years and estimated the amount at approximately $4.2 million annually.

dollar_amounts.context: estimated $4.2 million annually from consumers for services that should have been paid for with State and federal funds

findings.recommendation: We recommend that DDA determine the extent of the improperly collected CTC, as practical; and present this issue and basis for its decision to the General Assembly for its consideration.

findings.title: DDA did not adequately monitor the resource/service coordinators’ efforts to determine whether they were ensuring that consumers received the required services from providers and that Medicaid eligibility reassessments were conducted timely.
findings.description: DDA did not adequately monitor resource/service coordinators to ensure consumers received required medical, habilitative, or rehabilitative services as stipulated in individual service plans. DDA also failed to ensure annual Medicaid eligibility reassessments were performed timely for all consumers.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DDA verify, at least on a test basis, that the resource/service coordinators are effectively monitoring to ensure services are provided as required in the ISPs and that adequate documentation is maintained; follow up with providers to ensure corrective actions were taken for issues noted during site visits; ensure that ISPs are completed in accordance with State regulations; ensure that annual eligibility reassessments of consumers are performed, as required by federal regulations; and determine if eligibility can be restored to the consumers who lost Medicaid eligibility because reassessments were not timely performed.

findings.title: DDA did not compare hours billed by the resource/service coordinators with hours worked as recorded in its PCIS2 to ensure payments were proper.
findings.description: DDA did not adequately review the propriety of resource/service coordinators’ invoices prior to payment. A review of 15 invoices totaling $18.7 million disclosed that 12 invoices approved and paid had differences between hours billed and hours worked recorded in PCIS2, resulting in overpayments and underpayments.

dollar_amounts.context: aggregating approximately $538,000 in overpayments and underpayments

findings.recommendation: We recommend that DDA compare the hours billed by the resource/service coordinators with the hours worked as recorded in PCIS2 to ensure payments are only made for hours worked, and investigate any differences identified.

findings.title: DDA did not negotiate the contract rates for either contract, and DDA procured the second contract as an emergency procurement even though certain services ultimately provided under the contract did not appear to be emergencies as defined by regulation.
findings.description: DDA did not negotiate contract rates proposed by the vendor for two financial restructuring contracts. Additionally, DDA procured the second contract as an emergency procurement even though the actual services performed did not appear to constitute an emergency under State regulations.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DDA negotiate vendor proposed rates when only one responsive bid is received, and ensure that emergency procurements are only used for emergency situations as defined by regulation.

findings.title: DDA lacked an effective means to monitor payments for contract deliverables, and similar deliverables were included in both contracts and in certain contract modifications.
findings.description: DDA lacked an effective means to ensure payments were commensurate with the completion of contract deliverables. The contracts did not establish the vendor’s anticipated effort to complete related tasks, and similar deliverables were noted in both contracts raising questions about duplicate funding.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DDA include the anticipated effort to complete deliverables in its contracts to enable effective monitoring and to ensure the compensation for each successfully completed deliverable is limited to the agreed-upon hours; and compare the overall contract payments with the deliverables received, investigate any potentially duplicate payments and, in consultation with the Office of the Attorney General, pursue recovery of any such payments.

findings.title: DDA did not effectively monitor the contracts and the related payments. Certain deliverables were not received, vendor invoices were not effectively reviewed, and DDA authorized the contractor to perform work outside the scope of the contracts.
findings.description: DDA did not effectively monitor contracts to ensure deliverables were received or tasks completed. Three of four tested deliverables were not received despite full payment. Additionally, DDA paid for unapproved vendor employees and authorized work outside contract scope without modification.

dollar_amounts.context: paid $314,000 for three employees but lacked documentation that the employees had been approved to work

findings.recommendation: We recommend that DDA establish a formal process to ensure deliverables are received and to negotiate changes and modify related contracts to reduce costs when deliverables are determined to be no longer necessary; in consultation with the Attorney General, determine the feasibility of recovering contract costs for deliverables that were not received on the aforementioned contracts; obtain the required status reports with sufficient detail to assist in reviewing invoices and compliance with contract terms; ensure payments are not made for unapproved vendor employees; and seek contract modifications for services authorized beyond the scope of the related contracts.

findings.title: Federal fund reimbursement requests were not made timely, resulting in lost interest income totaling approximately $210,000.
findings.description: Federal fund reimbursement requests were not always submitted timely, resulting in lost interest income to the State of approximately $210,000 related to expenditures incurred during the period from July 2011 through June 2015. Portions of tested requests totaling $92 million were submitted late.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DDA ensure that future requests for federal fund reimbursement are submitted timely.

findings.title: DDA did not conduct audits of Community Supported Living Arrangement providers to identify and recover overpayments.
findings.description: DDA did not conduct audits of Community Supported Living Arrangement (CSLA) providers to identify and recover overpayments. The most recent contract with a vendor was terminated in January 2014, and DDA had not procured a replacement or directly conducted any audits during fiscal year 2015.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DDA consult with legal counsel to determine whether to take legal action against the auditor; ensure audits are conducted to verify the propriety of amounts paid to CSLA providers; and recover any overpayments identified through CSLA audits.

findings.title: DDA did not verify critical adjustments that were processed in PCIS2, resulting in errors such as overpayments going undetected, and did not adequately restrict access to the system.
findings.description: DDA had not established controls over critical adjustments to provider accounts which were manually processed without independent review. Tests identified two incorrect adjustments totaling $505,000. Additionally, DDA did not periodically review user access, with 9 of 10 tested users having unnecessary access.

dollar_amounts.context: two adjustments that were incorrectly processed by DDA employees totaling $505,000

findings.recommendation: We recommend that DDA establish independent review procedures to ensure the propriety, at least on a test basis, of critical adjustments processed in PCIS2; take immediate action to ensure that any improper adjustments identified are corrected and funds are recovered; perform a documented periodic review of user access capabilities to ensure that users are assigned only those capabilities needed to perform job duties; and eliminate unnecessary access.

findings.title: The PCIS2 database contained 58,022 unique social security numbers with associated names, dates of birth, and addresses without adequate safeguards.
findings.description: DDA inappropriately stored sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) in clear text within the PCIS2 database. As of August 28, 2015, the database contained 58,022 unique social security numbers with associated names, dates of birth, and addresses without adequate safeguards or encryption.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that DDA perform an inventory of its systems and identify all sensitive PII; determine if it is necessary to retain this PII and delete all unnecessary PII; determine if all necessary PII is properly protected by encryption or other substantial mitigating controls; and use approved encryption methods to encrypt all sensitive PII not otherwise properly protected.

extraction.agency_response_summary: The Department generally concurs with the audit recommendations, noting that some issues are ongoing or related to system transitions (e.g., PCIS2 to LTSS). The DDA does not concur with specific recommendations regarding recovering overpayments from past CSLA audits and duplicate contract payments due to data limitations.
extraction.extraction_notes: Total dollar impact calculated as sum of quantified amounts in findings: $4.2M (F1) + $538k (F3) + $314k (F6) + $210k (F7) + $505k (F9). Prior findings repeated count based on text summary stating 'remaining 3 findings are repeated' despite TOC showing 4 asterisks.
